coldOpen: Those copper dots on jeans started on horse blankets.
centralQuestion: Why do jeans have small copper rivets at the pocket corners?

sources.name: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Those Oft-Forgotten Pant Parts
Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Pockets Full of History

evidence.claim: Jacob Davis pioneered rivets on work trousers in 1871 while working as a tailor in Reno, Nevada.
evidence.quote: Jacob Davis pioneered rivets while working as a tailor in Reno
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Those Oft-Forgotten Pant Parts

evidence.claim: Davis had originally used rivets on horse blankets.
evidence.quote: Davis had originally used rivets on horse blankets
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Those Oft-Forgotten Pant Parts

evidence.claim: Rivets reinforced stress points such as back-pocket corners and the crotch, which often tore apart under heavy wear.
evidence.quote: particularly the corners of the back pockets and the crotch, which often tore apart when exposed to heavy duty wear and tear
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Those Oft-Forgotten Pant Parts

evidence.claim: Davis did not have the money to patent the technique, so he asked Levi Strauss to apply with him.
evidence.quote: Since Davis did not have the money required to patent the technique of using rivets
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Those Oft-Forgotten Pant Parts

evidence.claim: In 1873 the pair received a patent for an improvement in fastening pocket openings.
evidence.quote: the pair received a patent for “improvement in fastening pocket-openings.”
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Those Oft-Forgotten Pant Parts

evidence.claim: Copper rivets kept pockets from ripping and made the openings stronger.
evidence.quote: Copper rivets kept the pockets from ripping and made the openings stronger and more secure
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Pockets Full of History

evidence.claim: In 1937 Levi's began covering back-pocket rivets because the copper points scratched furniture and saddles.
evidence.quote: many had issues with the copper points scratching furniture and saddles
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Pockets Full of History

evidence.claim: The covered back-pocket rivets were dropped altogether by 1966 because they wore through the denim.
evidence.quote: by 1966 were ditched altogether because they continued to wear through even the toughest denim
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Pockets Full of History

evidence.claim: Rivets continue to strengthen the most vulnerable parts of jeans.
evidence.quote: rivets continue to strengthen and reinforce the most vulnerable parts of our jeans
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Those Oft-Forgotten Pant Parts
